conversation:
kevin: FYI - AcmeCorp reporting persistent 429s during morning surge. Dedicated pool not scaling up past minReplicas for ~7m. Customer traffic queued.

kevin: Observed: probe loop logs show repeated 'probe skipped - heartbeat mismatch' and controller decisions showing 'no headroom' even though GPU utilization on existing pods is >85%.

ops-bot: Alert: acme-prod-dedicated cluster - high 429 rate detected (rule:slo-429-p95). Ticket created: #TCK-4821

mira: Can you paste the probe/controller logs and the exact warm-pool config? rough repro steps ok too.

kevin: repro commands attached inline:
```
kubectl -n redwood get dedicatedpods acme-prod -o yaml
kubectl -n redwood logs deploy/autoscaler -c controller --since=10m | grep probe
```
logs snippet:
```
2026-03-15T09:02:11Z controller INFO probe: last_heartbeat=2026-03-15T09:01:30Z current=2026-03-15T09:02:11Z mismatch, skipping probe
2026-03-15T09:02:12Z controller INFO decision: minReplicas=2 headroom_calc=skipped
2026-03-15T09:04:05Z controller WARN attach-rate-limit: 429 from registry
```

alex: quick check - can you share metrics link for scale_decision_latency and probe_success_rate? Also, is the warm-pool agent on the nodes reporting any errors?

kevin: metrics: https://grafana.redwood/acme/d/scale?panel=autoscale (private link) - probe_success_rate drops to 0 around 09:01. warm-agent logs show repeated "heartbeat stale" entries.

jess: hmm. We've seen similar when agent clock drifted vs controller. If the agent's heartbeat timestamp is older than controller threshold it suppresses probes which blocks headroom calc. Could be NTP / time sync issue.

mira: good call. kevin - can you run `date -u` on a few nodes (controller pod, warm-agent pod, and one model server)? Also `kubectl exec` into warm agent and check `/var/log/ntp.log` or `chrony` status.

kevin: running now. Results:
controller pod: "2026-03-15T09:02:15Z"
warm-agent node: "2026-03-15T09:01:24Z"
model-server node: "2026-03-15T09:02:16Z"
chrony: syncing=false, stratum=16 on warm-agent (bad)

alex: that explains mismatch. controller thinks agent heartbeat is stale -> probes suppressed -> autoscaler doesn't see headroom -> no scaleup. Not a capacity/cost policy issue.

jess: mitigation steps: 1) restart chrony on warm-agent nodes, 2) force-restart warm-agent pod to re-register heartbeat, 3) temporarily bump minReplicas to 4 for AcmeCorp until all nodes stable.

kevin: applied mitigation 1 & 2 on affected nodes at 09:07. Chrony re-synced. Warm-agent heartbeats resumed.

ops-bot: Incident update: TCK-4821 - mitigation applied, monitoring for 30m.

mira: confirm scale behaviour?

kevin: by 09:09 we observed two additional replicas spin up, queue drained, 429 rate back to baseline by 09:12. Scaling decision latency graph shows decision -> provision delta improved.

jess: root cause: agent node time drift (chrony failed) causing heartbeat timestamps to appear stale to controller, which suppressed probe headroom calculations and prevented autoscale decisions.

mira: action items: (1) add node-level ntp/chrony healthcheck to node-exporter dashboards, (2) autoscaler: log more details when skipping probe due to heartbeat (include node id), (3) run cluster audit to find other nodes with stratum>=16.

kevin: notified customer and closed SR after confirming recovery. Will follow up with RFC for autoscaler telemetry.

jess: thanks all. marking resolved unless we see recurrence. :thumbsup:
